recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the temporary category model or add a duplicate source-changing commit for FHIR-50689; any separate audit of FHIR-45617 or FHIR-49953 should be handled under those issue keys.
issue_request: FHIR-50689 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and asked to revert the Vital Signs profile direction that moved vital-sign-specific identification from Observation.code to Observation.category, relying on FHIR-45617's decision not to make that change.
initial_application: No prior source commit explicitly named FHIR-50689. Commit 66a80b5fef2c43d4a46709f2a03b6d933063cb08 applied the controlling FHIR-45617 decision by moving the Vital Signs interoperability standard LOINC identifiers back from Observation.category to Observation.code and deleting observation-vitalsign-category. Combined-branch commit 77306523b255399153f826a0253a64b14382d3eb later fixed the remaining stale Text Summary/profile-summary and example remnants under FHIR-50705.
additional_context: FHIR-50705 makes the same category-vs-code objection and is already represented on the combined branch; FHIR-50392 records the rejected alternative of category-based specific vital-sign searches; FHIR-49953 is the same revert family; FHIR-54960 is a duplicate metadata cleanup issue. OO minutes record FHIR-50689 as Persuasive/Pre-applied and FHIR-50705 as Persuasive/Pre-applied.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source keeps only the broad observation-category#vital-signs classifier in Observation.category and places the profile-specific LOINC identifiers and bindings on Observation.code. Targeted stale-pattern searches found no remaining observation-vitalsign-category source, stale interoperability-category wording, or LOINC-coded Observation.category blocks under source/observation.
